ion actually used. This plugin answers both.
# dsh-mcp-skill-list
🇬🇧 **English** · 🇨🇳 简体中文
> 🔎 Two things a DSH profile never tells you at a glance: **what this machine is wired to**, and **w
hat a session actually used**. This plugin answers both.
## 🧭 What it does
1. **🔌 What is this machine wired to?** — every configured MCP server, every skill on disk, every ho

ok they declare.
2. **📊 What did this session actually use?** — every TOOL / MCP / SKILL / HOOK the
conversation called, summarised per session and per turn.
It ships two surfaces, both rendered as real React inside DSH slots (no iframe):
| Surface | Where |

| 🧩 **Inventory panel** | Sidebar icon + main panel, three tabs: MCP / SKILL / HOOK |
| 🧰 **Usage ta
b** | Conversation top bar, right after **Trajectory** (`轨迹`), labelled **工具** |
## 🧩 Inventory panel (left sidebar)
- **🔌 MCP** — server name, transport (`stdio` / `streamable-http`), the startup command line or endp
oint URL, environment **variable names only**, and whether tools from that server are currently regi

stered.
- **🎒 SKILL** — name, description, `whenToUse`, the provider that supplied it, its `SKILL.md

` path, and how many hooks it declares.
- **🪝 HOOK** — every hook declared by a skill's frontmatter,
plus anything in `~/.claude/settings.json`, `<cwd>/.claude/settings.json` and `settings.local.json`
, plus the eight events the host can hook into.
📋 Every name has a copy button.
## 🧰 Usage tab (conversation top bar)
Two levels, switched by a segmented control:
- **📊 Session summary** — every tool the session called, with call counts, error counts and the numb
er of turns it appeared in. Sub-tabs split TOOL / SKILL / MCP / HOOK; the hook tab also estimates ho

w many times each hook would have fired.
- **🪜 Turn detail** — one collapsible card per turn: the pr
ompt that opened it, its call count, and the tools / skills / MCP servers that turn used.
🧠 MCP tools are recognised by their `mcp__<server>__<tool>` names and grouped back to their server,
so you see *which MCP server did the work*, not just an opaque tool name.
## 🔌 Data sources
Everything is read, never written.
| Fact | Where it comes from |

| 🔌 MCP servers | profile Loader entries whose module is `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` |
| 🩺 MCP con

nectivity | `tools.schemas()` filtered by the `mcp__` prefix |
| 🎒 Skills | the `skills` service sna
pshot, backed by a disk scan of `~/.agents/skills`, `~/.dsh/skills`, `<cwd>/.agents/skills`, `<cwd>/

.dsh/skills` |
| 🪝 Hooks | `hooks:` frontmatter inside `SKILL.md`, plus Claude Code settings files |
| 📊 Session usage | the session event log via `sessionQuery` (`tool/call`, `tool/result`, `turn/sta
ion usage | the session event log via `sessionQuery` (`tool/call`, `tool/result`, `turn/start`, …) |
🔒 **Secrets stay home.** Environment variables are reduced to their key names before they ever leave
the host process; values are never serialised, never sent to the browser, never logged.

From the plugin market, one click. Or from a DSH session:

From a checkout:

## ✅ Requirements

- 🖥️ DSH runtime with the `web` platform (the panel is a web client plugin).
- 📦 No third-party runt
ime dependencies: the host half imports only `node:fs/promises`, `node:os` and `node:path`; the clie
nt half requires only `react` from the browser module table.
## 🗂️ Layout
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Two routes are registered on the host:

- `GET /api/dsh-mcp-skill-list/inventory` — 🧩 MCP servers, skills, hooks
- `GET /api/dsh-mcp-skill-l
ist/usage?sessionId=…` — 📊 per-session and per-turn usage
🛡️ Both reject non-loopback origins and cross-site requests.
## 🌐 UI language
The interface follows the DSH language setting out of the box — Simplified Chinese and English dicti
onaries are bundled in `locale/{zh,en}.json`, no extra configuration needed.
